newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc said on Wednesday it adopted a shareholder rights plan similar to a 10-year-old plan that expired earlier this month.

"Like our prior rights plan, the rights plan adopted today is designed to assure that all Caterpillar shareholders receive fair and equal treatment in the event of any proposed takeover of the company," Chairman Donald Fites said.

The rights will be exercisable if a person or group acquires 15 percent or more of the company's common stock, or announces a tender offer that would result in ownership of 15 percent or more of the company's stock, the heavy-equipment maker said.
The rights, which expire December 11, 2006, would allow Cateprillar shareholders to purchase stock at a 50 percent discount.
A spokesman said the plan was not in response to any specific takeover proposal.
Caterpillar shares fell 1-3/4 to 77 on the New York Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
